requirement.summary: Platform - HQ - Hide modules/functions without Read permission (Dev 2/2)
requirement.description:
User Story

As an Admin Console user, I want modules and functions I lack Read permission for to be hidden automatically so that the interface is less cluttered, I can focus only on what I am authorized to access, and I no longer encounter confusing "No Access" errors.

Current Behavior

All modules and functions in the Admin Console (HQ and LS) are displayed to every user regardless of their assigned permissions. When a user navigates to a page they do not have permission to view, they see a "No Access" error page, which causes confusion and friction. This has been cited negatively during feedback sessions with both internal and external stakeholders. Additionally, because permissions in the Admin Console are complex, end users struggle to understand what a specific user will or will not have access to during configuration.

Expected Behavior

A new setting "Hide Modules/Functions with no Access Rights" (On/Off, default Off) is added under System Management > System Configuration (Global Settings or User Module). When On, the system checks the logged-in user's Read permissions and hides modules/functions accordingly:

1. If a user has no Read permission for any function in a module, the entire module is hidden from navigation.

2. If a user has Read permission for at least one function in a module, the module is visible but only the permitted function(s) are shown; all other functions are hidden.

3. If a user has Read permission for a module itself but no Read permission for any of its child functions, the module is visible but displayed as empty or greyed out.

4. The feature takes effect only after the user logs out and logs back in after the setting is toggled.

5. Hidden modules/functions are also inaccessible via direct URL — navigating to a hidden module redirects to a "Page Not Found" page or the dashboard.

6. Any On/Off toggle of the setting is recorded in Audit Log with UserID, timestamp, and action.

7. The setting is configurable at zone level (Supreme, region, area) — individual properties can override the zone-level setting.

8. Any user with access to System Configuration can toggle the setting.

9. When the setting is toggled from On to Off, all modules and functions revert to the default visibility behavior (everything shown) after logout and re-login.

Acceptance Criteria

Setting visibility and toggle

- Given a user with access to System Configuration is logged into the Admin Console

- When they navigate to System Management > System Configuration

- Then a new setting 'Hide Modules/Functions with no Access Rights' (On/Off toggle, default Off) is visible

- And the user can toggle the setting On or Off

- And the toggle action is recorded in Audit Log with UserID, timestamp, and action (On or Off)

- But a user without access to System Configuration cannot see or modify this setting

Module hidden when no Read permission exists for any function

- Given the setting is On and a user has no Read permission for any function in the 'Reports' module

- When the user logs out and logs back in

- Then the 'Reports' module is not visible in the Admin Console navigation

- And navigating directly to any Reports URL redirects to a 'Page Not Found' page or the dashboard

- But the setting is Off, the 'Reports' module remains visible and navigating to it shows the 'No Access' error page as before

Partial module visibility when some Read permissions exist

- Given the setting is On and a user has Read permission for 'User Management > Create User' but not for 'User Management > Delete User'

- When the user logs out and logs back in

- Then the 'User Management' module is visible in navigation

- And the 'Create User' function is visible within the module

- But the 'Delete User' function is hidden within the module

- And navigating directly to the 'Delete User' URL redirects to a 'Page Not Found' page or the dashboard

Module visible but empty when no child function has Read permission

- Given the setting is On and a user has Read permission for a module but no Read permission for any of its child functions

- When the user logs out and logs back in

- Then the module is visible in navigation

- But the module appears empty or greyed out when opened, with no functions listed

Zone-level configuration with property override

- Given the setting is Off at Supreme zone but On at a specific region zone

- When a user under that region logs into the Admin Console

- Then the hiding behavior follows the region zone's setting (On)

- And a property under that region can independently override the region's setting

- But a property cannot override to a value that grants more visibility than its parent zone if the parent zone has the setting On and the property-level override is restricted by zone hierarchy rules

Setting Off restores default visibility

- Given the setting is toggled from On to Off

- When the user logs out and logs back in

- Then all modules and functions are displayed regardless of Read permissions, matching the current default behavior

- And previously hidden modules are accessible via direct URL and show their normal content

- But the visibility change does not take effect until logout and re-login; the current session retains the previous visibility state

Supporting Evidence

No additional supporting documents provided by requester. Original ticket: HERO-65825.

Requested Timeline

Aligned with Priority: Medium

Preferred Quarter: Not specified

Target Version: Not specified

Notes: No hard deadline provided by requester.

Alternatives Considered

Not specified by requester.

Original Description (preserved by INF Prod. Studio)

Enhancement Details

- Request to add a new setting "Hide Modules/Functions with no Access Rights", On/Off, default Off

- Hide modules/functions lack of Read permission

Setting Details

- Location: System Management > System Configuration > Global Settings (or under User Module)

- Support both HQ and LS

- Available from Supreme zone, but lower config zones can override the Supreme level independently

- When On: The system will check all the user's Read permissions and will hide the modules/functions accordingly:

1. If a user has no Read permission for a module, the whole module will be invisible in the backend

2. If a user has Read permission for one function in a module, the module will be visible and only that function within the module is visible, the rest of the functions will be invisible as they don't have Read Permission

- The feature takes effect only after user turn on the setting then logs out and logs back in

- Any On/Off actions of the setting will be recorded in Audit Log with UserID, time, action

- User Authority: Users who are authorized to access to System Configuration

_______________________________________________________________________________________________

Current Behaviour:

Infrasys has a lot of modules/functions which are displayed to all users with access to the Admin Console regardless of their permissions. This is confusing to new users and also presents a very cluttered and complicated appearance of the application to the end user. This has been mentioned in a negative light during feedback sessions with both internal and external stakeholders. As permissions in the Admin Console are complex some end users also complain it is hard to understand what a specific user will/wont have access to when doing configuration.

Currently, when a user opens a page they do not have permission to view they see this error which causes additional friction.

Expected Behaviour:

The system should automatically hide any modules/functions in the Admin console based on the access rights permissions of the logged-in user when the new setting is set to 'On'.

Setting Behaviour:

- A new setting 'Hide Modules/Functions with no Access Rights' (On/Off) shall be added, defaulting to Off.

- The new setting should be located in System Management > System Configuration > either under Global Settings or User Module.

- The setting should be applicable in both HQ and LS environments.

- The setting should be available from the Supreme config zone (to apply to all lower config zones automatically if enabled) - however the option to 'override' the setting at a lower config zone should also be possible.

- When Off: The system continues using the existing display behaviour that all Modules/Functions are visible to logged-in users regardless of Access Rights.

- When turned On: The system checks the existing user permission of 'Read' to decided what parts of the Admin console the user should see.

-

- For Example - if they User as no 'Read' permissions for any function under the 'Messaging' module then the entire module and all sub-headings should be hidden in the UI.

- If the user has 'Read' permission for one or more functions under the 'Messaging' module then the module heading should be shown along with the relevant functions - but any functions with no 'Read' permission should remain hidden.

- The action of turning the setting on or off should be logged in the Audit Log, capturing the operator's User ID and the timestamp of the action, and if the setting was turned on or off.

User Stories:

As an IT manager - I can clearly see what sections I have access to, without any necessary information showing on my Admin console UI. This means my UI is uncluttered. I can also quickly see if a user reports having no access to a required feature/module as it will not be displayed on their UI.

As a System Master - My UI will only display Modules/Functions that I have access rights to, it will make my experience in the Admin console easier to navigate and less prone to cause confusion with displaying lots of unrelated information that I cannot access or use at my property.

As an Implementations Specialist - I can test my user access rights setting/configuration more easily as I can make test users that will clearly show what sections are accessible based on the users' permission without having to open each function page.

Enhancements: [Jira-68451] Platform - HQ - Hide modules/functions without Read permission (Dev 2/2)
Description:
A new setting, "Function Permission Filter," has been added. When enabled, the navigation will be hidden if a user does not have "Read" permission for it.
If all functions under a group or module tab have no “Read” permission, hide the entire group or module tab.
Both HQ and LS support this enhancement.
Setup:
Add a new option in system settings: "Function Permission Filter", which is "Disable" by default.
The "Function Permission Filter" has the following special limitations and settings:
This setting can only be configured in the supreme config zone and by users with the roles of "System Administrator".
After enabling/disabling the settings, the navigation hiding/showing function will take effect after refreshing the page (currently logged in).
If the "Function Permission Filter" setting is changed, the prompts at the child level will take effect after the user logs in again.
Users can use different permission settings in different config zone to control whether the navigation is shown or hidden.
If a sub navigation cannot be set in user access control, then even if "All Access Rights = No Read" is set, the sub navigation and the parent navigation will still be displayed.
"Function Permission Filter" settings cannot be overridden.
"Function Permission Filter" settings does not support publishing from HQ to LS.
If the navigation cannot be set with permissions, it is not supported to hide it.
Whether the menu is hidden or shown will change depending on the following actions:
User access control updated.
Adding/ Removing user from user group.
The setting is toggled.
Once enabled, a message will appear below Functions stating "Unauthorized functions are hidden".
In the user access control settings, select a user and add a new permission setting record. Under the "Display Screens" sub-menu in "Digital Signage", do not select the "read" permission.
Menus without read permission will be hidden.
